facts.claim: A network of coastal lakes, marshes and lagoons in East Gippsland covering about 354 km2 between Lakes Entrance, Bairnsdale and Sale.
The largest lakes are Wellington, King and Victoria, fed by the Avon, Thomson, Latrobe, Mitchell, Nicholson and Tambo rivers.
Ninety Mile Beach, just over 151 km long, separates the lakes from Bass Strait; the lakes drain to the sea through a short man-made canal at Lakes Entrance.
The lakes can be explored by cruise, water taxi, or boat and kayak hire; bream, flathead and trevally are popular catches, with jetties and ramps at Paynesville, Lakes Entrance and Metung.
About 50 of the rare Burrunan dolphin live in the lakes, which are a Ramsar-listed wetland with two protected areas, The Lakes National Park and Gippsland Lakes Coastal Park.
Lakes Entrance, the largest town (about 4,500 people), sits beside a footbridge to the Ninety Mile Beach surf beach, patrolled each summer.

tips.title: Summer beach patrols
tips.detail: Eastern Beach at Lakes Entrance is patrolled between Christmas and Australia Day; swim between the flags.

tips.title: Summer crowds
tips.detail: The lakeside tourist towns swell in summer, so book accommodation ahead for December to February.

best_months.rationale: Boating, fishing and swimming peak in summer when the towns swell and beaches are patrolled; the sources give no further seasonal detail.

wikivoyage_page: no (https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Gippsland_Lakes returns no page); Lakes Entrance has one: https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lakes_Entrance

facts.claim: Hamilton is a town in western Victoria, on the A200 Henty Highway, and calls itself the Wool Capital of the World for its sheep-grazing history.
The surrounding shire produces as much as 15% of Australia's wool clip.

Hamilton Botanic Gardens were designed in 1881 by William Guilfoyle, director of the Royal Botanic Gardens Melbourne, and feature rare plants, a restored rotunda, the Thomson Fountain and a small zoo.
The Sir Reginald Ansett Transport Museum displays the airline's first aircraft, a Fokker Universal, with models, vehicles and memorabilia.
Wannon Falls, a 30 m punchbowl waterfall about 19 km west of Hamilton, drops over a basalt cliff into a plunge pool.
Grampians National Park is a short drive away.

tips.title: Falls flow in winter
tips.detail: Wannon Falls is best in the winter wet and can shrink to a trickle by the end of summer.

tips.title: Reach it by road
tips.detail: Hamilton is on the Henty Highway, served by V/Line coaches, and its airport takes only recreational aircraft.

best_months.rationale: Wannon Falls is spectacular in the winter wet and weak after the summer dry; no other seasonal source found.

note: Name collision with NZ 'Hamilton'; owner to confirm disambiguated name.

facts.claim: Portland, on Portland Bay, is the oldest European settlement in Victoria; Edward Henty landed there in November 1834 and sowed the state's first wheat crop.
It has more than 200 historical buildings from the 1800s, and a waterfront where ships load local produce and the fishing fleet lands its catch.
The Maritime Discovery Centre shows whaling and shipwreck history, with a sperm whale skeleton and a Portland lifeboat from the 1850s.
Cape Bridgewater has up to 650 fur seals, the highest coastal cliff in Victoria, a blowhole and limestone tubes called the petrified forest.
Southern right whales can be seen from Cape Bridgewater's cliffs in winter and spring.
The 251 km Great South West Walk begins and ends at the Portland Visitor Information Centre and passes through forest, river gorge, cliff tops and bays, with options for day walks.
The Portland Cable Tram runs from Henty Park to the World War 2 Memorial Lookout.

experiences: Walk the Great South West Walk
See fur seals and whales at the capes

tips.title: Whale season
tips.detail: Southern right whales pass Cape Bridgewater in winter and spring, and often visit Portland Bay in winter.

tips.title: Day-walk the big track
tips.detail: The 251 km Great South West Walk has shorter sections, accessed from roads near Portland and Nelson.

best_months.rationale: Southern right whales are seen in winter and spring; the walks have no further seasonal source.

facts.claim: Phillip Island lies at the mouth of Western Port, about 140 km and two hours from Melbourne, and is joined to the mainland by a 640 m bridge from San Remo to Newhaven.
About 40,000 little penguins live on the island, and the Penguin Parade at Summerland Beach has run since the 1920s, with visitors watching them come ashore at dusk.
Seal Rocks, off the Nobbies at the western end, hosts Australia's largest fur seal colony, up to about 16,000.
The island is home to a koala conservation centre with tree-top boardwalks, and Churchill Island, site of Victoria's first European farm (1801), is joined by a bridge.
Australia's first Grand Prix was held on the island in 1928, and the 1956 Grand Prix Circuit hosts MotoGP and Superbikes.
Victoria's first National Surfing Reserve (2013) covers Woolamai, Smiths Beach, Summerlands and Cat Bay.
The permanent population of 13,799 swells to about 40,000 in summer.

experiences: Watch penguins come ashore at dusk
See fur seals and wild coastline

tips.title: Penguin times vary
tips.detail: Penguins arrive about 5:15pm in June to 8:45pm in January. Viewing areas are outdoors, so bring warm, wind-proof layers.

tips.title: Bring a car
tips.detail: The island has little public transport, none to the Penguin Parade, and the Nobbies are over five hours' walk from Newhaven.

tips.title: Avoid night driving
tips.detail: Skip unpaved roads at night, as kangaroos and wallabies jump out; slow right down if you must drive.

best_months.rationale: Mild, fairly dry summers (highs about 24 C in February versus 13.5 C in July), when the island is busiest.
